chunks: From him, from Safwan, from Hakam ibn Hukeym who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): A person died and had not performed Hajj and did not bequeath that Hajj be performed, so one of his family members, a man or a woman, performed Hajj on his behalf. Would that suffice, and serve as a discharge (Qaza) for him, and would the Hajj be for the one who performed it, and would the one who performed it on his behalf be rewarded? He (peace be upon him) said: If the pilgrim was not Sarurah (one who has already performed Hajj), it would suffice for both of them together, and the reward would be for the one who performed his Hajj.

key_terms.صُرُورَةٍ: One who has already performed their obligatory Hajj
key_terms.قَضَاءً: Discharge or fulfillment of an obligation

ai.seo_question: Does performing Hajj on behalf of a deceased person who didn't bequeath it count for them and reward the performer?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the permissibility of voluntary Hajj (Hajj al-Tatawwu') serving as discharge for the obligatory Hajj (Fard) of a deceased person who died without bequeathing funds, a key distinction in Shia fiqh. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that if the performer is not 'Sarurah' (one who has already completed their own obligatory Hajj), the act suffices for the deceased while the performer retains their own reward, highlighting the dual benefit of voluntary acts in Shia jurisprudence. This ruling underscores the importance of family members fulfilling religious duties on behalf of the dead when no specific bequest exists, a practice widely accepted among the Shia school.
